subject: Technical fit: latency & throughput checklist
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Li <amy@finlytics.com>, John Chen <john.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Technical fit: latency & throughput checklist

Thanks for the time today — quick follow-up to capture the technical constraints we discussed so the PoC scope is clear. Below is a concise checklist based on today's call; please flag anything I missed and attach the small traffic sample you mentioned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- UI feels sluggish during live sessions: first-token latency ranges ~600–900ms today (hosted model).
- Spikes during earnings windows cause user-facing stalls; you see brief congestion at ~900–1200 concurrent sessions.
- Cost per conversation is high because of repeated full-model calls for short prompts (prefix reuse not implemented).

Current stack (from call):
- Frontend: React app with streaming (EventSource) for partial updates.
- Backend: Node service calling hosted LLM provider for text generation + Redis for session state.
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana (sample metrics request attached).

Success criteria (what FinLytics needs to consider PoC-successful):
- First-token p95 <= 250ms for interactive assistant flows (50–100 token responses).
- Sustained concurrency support to 400 sessions with ability to absorb spikes to ~1.2k for short periods.
- 20–30% reduction in per-conversation token cost via prefix/KV caching or batching.

Proposed Redwood PoC checklist / next steps:
1) FinLytics: share 72h traffic sample (event timestamps, payload sizes, request concurrency profile) — we can use the CSV format I attached as a template.
2) Redwood: provision a dedicated proof-of-concept pool (best-effort match to your expected GPUs) and run a synthetic replay against your sample traffic.
3) Joint test plan: evaluate (a) first-token p95, (b) median tokens/sec, (c) tail CPU/GPU utilization, (d) cost per 1k tokens.
4) Timeline: aim to kick-off week of 2027-06-21. 2-week run + 1-week analysis.
5) Logistics: provide short-term access tokens for telemetry replay, and a privileged read-only S3/Drive path for metrics logs.

Attachments: traffic_snapshot_72h.csv (template), prometheus_sample.json (metric scrape), Redwood PoC proposal (PDF).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a one-page PoC mutual action plan and proposed dates.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Amy Li <amy@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Chen <john.chen@finlytics.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-07T18:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Technical fit: latency & throughput checklist

Thanks Karthik — this looks right and very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: we attached the anonymized 72h traffic CSV you suggested.

Questions / clarifications:
- Our "first-token" measurement today is taken at the browser when the EventSource yields the initial chunk; is that the same point Redwood will measure? We want apples-to-apples.
- Typical response lengths for interactive assistant sessions are 40–120 tokens; however, our doc-synthesis jobs are longer (400–800 tokens) and can be batched offline. The PoC should focus on the interactive flows.
- Concurrency: our baseline during normal hours is ~250 concurrent active sessions; spikes to 1.2k happen during earnings release minutes (5–10 minutes window). We need graceful degradation during spikes (queueing/fallback) rather than hard failures.

Constraints:
- No production data can leave our VPC; we can provide a sanitized telemetry drop in Drive.
- We need a simple cost projection for projected monthly QPS before committing to dedicated capacity.

I copied John who will confirm the traffic freeze windows so we can coordinate a replay.

—Amy
Head of Product, FinLytics

Attachment: finlytics_traffic_72h_anonymized.csv

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Li <amy@finlytics.com>, John Chen <john.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-08T08:15:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Technical fit: latency & throughput checklist

Appreciate the quick response and the CSV. Short answers inline and proposed commitments below.

Measurement point: we will instrument the PoC with an agent that emits both (a) server-side first-token time (when token leaves GPU runtime) and (b) synthetic browser-side timing via the replay harness. We will correlate to ensure apples-to-apples.

PoC focus: agreed — prioritize interactive flows (40–120 tokens). We will run a secondary longer-run to validate batching for doc-synthesis but keep it separate.

Concurrency & graceful degradation: Redwood can configure a tiered fallback policy — canary model variants + queued headroom + immediate short text fallback. For the PoC we will exercise a policy that preserves first-token p95 for 90% of traffic and routes overflow to a lower-cost variant.

Redwood commitments for PoC (what we will demonstrate):
- Target: first-token p95 <= 250ms on interactive flows under sustained 400 concurrent sessions.
- Spike handling: demonstrate handling of 1.2k spike for short windows with graceful fallback (observable in Grafana dashboard).
- Cost estimation: provide a projected per-1k-token cost based on your traffic, plus a delta showing savings from KV caching and batching.

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- FinLytics (John): confirm week-of 2027-06-21 for kickoff and share Drive link for telemetry (by 2027-06-11).
- Redwood (Karthik/Ben): prepare PoC cluster config and provide a one-page mutual action plan (by 2027-06-10).
- Joint: schedule 30-min kickoff to align metrics and success criteria (target date 2027-06-22).

If that all looks good I’ll drop a short Workback and a proposed schedule into HubSpot and Drive.

Best,
Karthik

Action items for our side:

- Lauren: schedule kickoff 2027-06-22 11:00 ET provisional.

Thanks — Lauren
